source.title: The Hidden Power of Normalization Layers in Neural Networks: Exponential Capacity Control

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text contains the full paper.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains two CIFAR-10 models from He initialization and reports training accuracy, bearing on whether training reaches near-zero training error. It does not compare the training recipes or conditions named in the other versions.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports weight norms and input variances, but these do not measure the training-error behavior named in the claim versions. Cited results from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The ResNet18 experiment directly measures training classification accuracy on CIFAR-10 using Adam from random initialization, matching V1's method and measure. The fully connected ReLU network falls outside V1's convolutional-network scope.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate, but the conclusions are conditional theoretical claims: under large input variances, normalization can exponentially reduce Lipschitz bounds, improve stationarity-complexity bounds, and tighten generalization bounds. The analysis omits normalization's affine scale and shift parameters. The experiments illustrate weight norms, activation variances, and training accuracy; they do not compare optimization performance with and without normalization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains models on CIFAR-10 with Adam, He normal initialization, and 100 epochs; it does not test the full range of datasets, labels, optimizers, or model sizes in V1.

fits_no_version.finding: Training accuracy of a 10-layer fully connected ReLU network on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient training can approach zero training classification error in fully connected ReLU networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Corollary 19 gives stationarity evaluation-complexity upper bounds with a BN-dependent factor of sigma^(-K+i-1), under large-variance assumptions. These bounds do not establish a measured accuracy-speed advantage or a separation in actual convergence times.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the paper's assumptions, BN can reduce theoretical upper bounds on evaluations needed to reach approximate stationarity.

record.problems: Training accuracy is shown only in figures, without numerical values or uncertainty. The text's statement that training error approaches zero is not attributed to individual models, and no comparison tests the listed failure conditions.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; two training-accuracy results are included. Other plotted quantities, such as weight norms and activation variances, do not measure the behavior named by the versions.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, SGD, model-size comparisons, early-stopping effects, and comparisons of regularized recipes. Weight decay is used, but its effect is not isolated.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious-minimum frequencies, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error comparisons across depths and between plain and residual networks; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Comparative training speed or trainable depth under different initializations.
Loss and curvature trajectories relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Accuracy gained per training time or iteration with versus without BN, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied figure extraction contains axes and captions but no readable curve endpoints. The V1 verdict consequently rests on the qualitative statement in Section 4.2. He initialization alone does not test V4, and Lipschitz or stationarity bounds alone do not establish V6's accuracy-speed and learning-rate claims.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, SGD, smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes are not tested.
